title: constraint compiler: lexical-boundary stability shim for regex/cfg backends and OpenAI compat
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add constraint compiler that aligns CFG/regex constraints to tokenizer boundaries with streaming-safe framing and OpenAI-compatible function_call/tool_call mapping. Backward-compatible; behavior exposed behind feature flag.
description:
Motivation: our constrained decoding backends (CFG and regex) have orthogonal semantics around token boundaries which led to intermittent streaming fragmentation, tool-call framing mismatches in the OpenAI compat layer, and surprising rejections for user-provided regexes that operate on byte/character spans. This PR introduces a small, opt-in "constraint compiler" that compiles grammar and regex constraint specs into a tokenizer-aware intermediate automaton and a streaming-stability shim. The compiler's goals are: 1) preserve original constraint semantics at the character level where authors expect it, 2) avoid emitting partial-token fragments during streaming, 3) provide deterministic fallback behavior when constraints cross tokenizer subtokens, and 4) make the OpenAI compatibility layer (function_call/tool_call) robust to these subtleties.

Implementation summary:
- New compiler module (go/decoder/constraint_compiler.go and go/decoder/automaton/*) that ingests CFG rules and regex patterns and emits a token-anchored automaton plus a small set of rewrite hints (preferred delimiter tokens, safe lookahead windows). The compiler maintains a mapping table from UTF-8 byte spans to tokenizer subtoken indices so regex anchors and character classes are preserved as closely as feasible.
- Streaming stability shim: when emitting streamed chunks the runtime consults the automaton's safe-lookahead window; if a constraint boundary would split a tokenizer subtoken we buffer up to N bytes (configurable, default 32) and emit a special checkpoint-marker token that is guaranteed to be tokenizer-aligned. This avoids producing incomplete toolcall frames or truncated structured outputs over gRPC/HTTP streaming. The shim is conservative by default and relaxes heuristics under low-latency policies.
- OpenAI compat layer changes (js/openai_compat/func_call_shim.ts): function_call outputs are now post-processed using the compiler's rewrite hints so that tool/function names and JSON argument frames are framed at token boundaries and safe for downstream JSON parsers. A small translator maps compiled automaton events to the OpenAI function_call schema when a user requests openai_compat: true.
- Fallbacks & safety: when the compiler detects an inexpressible constraint (e.g., lookbehind across variable-width encodings), it records a deterministic fallback: either approximate by token-prefix matching or degrade to regex-only at the cost of potential extra rejections. Users can opt-out via the existing constrain.enable_compiler flag.
- Tests and benchmarks: added python/js/go e2e tests (python/tests/test_constraint_streaming.py, js/tests/openai_compat_toolcall.test.ts) covering: regex with multi-byte chars, CFG rules that anchor mid-token, streaming reassembly across chunk boundaries, and toolcall framing under high throughput. Microbenchmarks show ~<3% median token latency increase under default conservative buffering and up to 12% when forcing maximal boundary checks; typical throughput remains within SLA for dedicated pools.
- Docs and examples: docs/structured-output/constraint-compiler.md documents behavior, flags, and migration notes. The PR also adds a short recipe demonstrating how to author regexes that are compiler-friendly.

Commits:
- feat(compiler): add constraint compiler core and automaton serializer
- feat(streaming): add safe-lookahead buffering and checkpoint-marker emission
- feat(compat): integrate compiler hints into OpenAI function_call shim
- fix(tests): add e2e and unit tests for multibyte regex and toolcall framing
- perf: tune automaton cache eviction and add benchmark harness
- docs: add constraint-compiler usage and migration notes

Files changed (high level): go/decoder/constraint_compiler.go go/decoder/automaton/regex_compiler.go go/decoder/automaton/serializer.go go/serving/streaming/shim.go js/openai_compat/func_call_shim.ts python/tests/test_constraint_streaming.py js/tests/openai_compat_toolcall.test.ts docs/structured-output/constraint-compiler.md infra/ci/constraint_compiler.yml benchmarks/constraint_compiler/README.md benchmarks/constraint_compiler/run.sh Makefile (benchmarks)

Notable snippets:
- tokenizer-alignment table generation (go/decoder/constraint_compiler.go): a compact map of byte-span->subtoken-index used at compile time and embedded as a sparse table in the automaton header.
- streaming checkpoint marker emission (go/serving/streaming/shim.go): emits a stable delimiter token id (reserved range) rather than raw bytes to guarantee downstream parsers remain aligned.

Review summary:
- Diego: requested stronger test coverage for emojis and combining characters; asked to quantify buffering cost under large-batch continuous-stream workloads.
- Lina: requested an explicit migration note for Dedicated customers and suggested exposing the conservative buffer size as a runtime knob in the console.
- Evan: ran perf harness and suggested caching compiled automata keyed by constraint hash + tokenizer version to reduce CPU on hot paths.

Changes after review:
- Added python/js tests for emoji+combining sequences.
- Exposed runtime knob constrain.compiler.buffer_size (default 32) and console flag wiring in a follow-up patch from redwood-console team.
- Implemented automaton cache keyed by (constraint_hash, tokenizer_v) and added eviction policy with metrics.

CI: initial integration run had a flaky e2e failing under ephemeral network condition; rerun passed all checks:
- build: pass
- unit test: pass
- integration: pass (rerun)
- lint: pass
- benchmarks: pass

Merge: merged via squash by Lina Zhao.

Migration/risk notes:
- Feature is behind flag; zero user-visible change until teams opt in.
- Conservative defaults ensure no regressions for existing constraints but may slightly increase end-to-end latency for strict streaming policies; documented in release notes.
- Follow-ups: link console flag, add admin telemetry for constraint compiler adoption and fallback rates, and add an opt-in deterministic-mode that forces exact character-level semantics at higher cost.
